athlete: Matt Richards, James Guy, Jack McMillan, Duncan Scott (final); Evan Jones, Tom Dean (heats only)
evidence: Roster split, no clear majority: Richards - Wikipedia: 'Although born in England, Richards represented Wales as his father was born there' -> Wales. Guy - born Bury, England; Wikipedia 'Representing England' (Commonwealth Games) -> England. McMillan - born Belfast, County Antrim, Northern Ireland; Wikipedia Commonwealth Games record 'Representing' Northern Ireland -> Northern Ireland. Scott - born Glasgow, Scotland; Wikipedia Commonwealth Games infobox 'Representing Scotland' (13 Commonwealth Games medals for Scotland across three Games) -> Scotland. Jones (heats only) - Wikipedia: 'born in Scotland to English parents'; Commonwealth Games infobox 'Representing Scotland' (2022 Birmingham bronze medals in relays) -> Scotland. Dean (heats only) - 'Representing England' (see 2022 file) -> England. Combined six-swimmer roster (heats + final) splits exactly 2 England (Guy, Dean), 2 Scotland (Scott, Jones), 1 Wales (Richards), 1 Northern Ireland (McMillan) - a genuine tie between England and Scotland with no majority, and even restricting to the four final-race swimmers it is a four-way tie of one each (Wales, England, Northern Ireland, Scotland). Tie broken in favour of Scotland on the grounds that Duncan Scott swam the decisive anchor leg and posted the fastest individual split of the field (1:43.82), securing the gold; England (via Guy/Dean) is the equally defensible alternative apportionment. Flagged as moderate confidence given the genuine roster tie. [FRACTIONAL APPORTIONMENT: revised from winner-take-all majority rule to shares proportional to final-race roster composition, per repo-wide policy change following the Wales/NI audit (see data/olympics/WALES_NI_AUDIT.md) — smaller home nations contributing a minority of a mixed relay were previously rounded down to zero.]
